Text_en: National PHEOC/EOC ready for activation/activated, SOPs, roles and responsibilities, communication trees, etc are updated, disseminated and understood
Members of the national multisectoral coordination committee (or task force) are listed with clear terms of reference (including fund raising) and ready for activation
Cholera focal points (national and subnational) are listed/named in all cholera hotspots with clear terms of reference and ready to be deployed (or take up the role)
National long term cholera elimination plan is being developed/updated
Cholera hotspot districts have a multi-sectoral emergency coordination mechanism, with clear terms of reference and a designated coordinator and a contact list in place
4Ws (multisectoral) of partners is updated regularly (at least once quarterly) and shared with partners supporting cholera activities
Matrix for coordination of cholera control activities is shared with partners supporting cholera activities
Multidisciplinary Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) are listed out, trained, have a clear terms of reference and ready to be deployed
Multidisciplinary RRTs are fully equipped, have logistical support and ready to be deployed within 24 hours of notification
At least 1 fully equipped RRT and ready for immediate deployment in the cholera hotspot areas
All RRTs have SOPs/Guidelines/protocols for investigation, diagnosis, risk assessment, case management
Public health personnel are listed out, trained on latest IDSR in the hotspot areas (high risk areas) and all POEs
Public health facilities in the hotspot areas (high risk areas) and all POEs are prompt in reporting and informing of potential epidemic diseases including acute watery diarrhoea cases through IDSR
Cholera case definitions are updated and disseminated to all levels of health care system including community level
Community volunteers are trained on cholera surveillance (CBS-event and indicator based) and reporting in the hotspot areas (high risk areas) and POEs
Private sector in hotspot areas (high risk) are listed out and trained on cholera surveillance and report into local health authority
Cholera risk assessment/mapping is done annually and used to prioritize readiness in hotspots
RDT supplies are calculated based on expected attack rates in hotspot districts and ready to be deployed/prepositioned to hotspots
Cary-Blair transport medium is available according to projected number of cases in referral laboratories in district hotspots
Carey-Blair transport medium is available in the facility in cholera hotspot areas?
The national reference laboratoy has the capacity for both culture techniques and drug susceptibility testing or have MoU with international lab for this service
SOPs for collection, packaging, and transport of samples are available in all laboratories in hotspot areas (high risk)
Listing of health care personnel trained in safe sample collection and packaging is updated
Country has a functional system for reporting (laboratory results) to stakeholders (health workers and health authorities)

Essential laboratory supplies and consumables (RDTs, Enteric disease bacteriological kits, stains etc) are estimated according to at risk populations in hotspot areas and pre-positioned or procured with known lead times
Country has capacity to sequence circulating vibrio cholera or agreement/MoU with international laboratory
All POEs in hot spot areas are fully equipped and have trained staff capable of managing cholera cases
Public health authorities, companies in the PoE (air, sea and road) are sensitized to cholera prevention, case detection, treatment, notification and referral systems
All POE have functioning latrines and hand hygiene facilities (Functioning meaning soap/ABHR and water present)
Posters and leaflets for traveller health education are made available in all PoEs (translated into local and traveller languages)

Identify/make ready the health facilitie/services including CTU/CTC/ORPs and temporary treatment sites with updated case management protocols and adequate infrastructure, supplies and equipment for AWD/Cholera clinical response in hotspots
Surge health personnel (repurposing/recruited/medical colleges etc) trained in managing cholera cases are listed out and ready for deployment/repurposing
Heath personnel (current) in health facilities in hotspots received refresher training in case managment of cholera patients
Community volunteers are trained in community management of cholera patients in ORPs
Functioning system in place for referral of cholera patients at all levels
Updated clinical guidelines on IPC and management of cholera patient is available
At least 80% Health workers in hotspots (high-risk areas) are trained/received refresher training in IPC and SDB protocol
At least 80% of health facilities in hotspots (high-risk areas) have cholera infection prevention and control guidelines and SOPs
At least 80% of community volunteers have been identified and trained in hygeine promotion and preparation of disinfection solutions in hotspots (high risk areas)
At least 80% of community based-volunteers are trained in conducting household disinfection in hotspot areas
Safe and dignified burial protocol is avaialbe in all facilities
SDB teams are listed, shared and trained in SDB procedure
Projections of WASH/IPC needs are finalized based on proper use of PPE, WASH requirements based on risk levels at designated health facilities (all levels) in identified hotspots
Country has designated and trained spokespersons on epidemic communication

Participatory approach adopted to develop RCCE messages (in the local language) on risk mitigation measure/control strategies, tested and disseminated via preferred public medias (radio, TV) for maximum exposure.
Community volunteers in hotspots are selected by the community and trained in key messages for colera prevention and control
List of designated health facilities and temporary treatment sites in hotspots (high risk)has been updated for managing cholera cases in CTC/CTU/ORP
Workforce is avaialbe and trained in setting up CTC/CTUs and integrated cholera management
At least 1 CTCs/ CTUs is pre-postioned/available in each hotspot districts
Minimal stock of cholera response supplies are prepositioned based on the forecasting tool at designated hotspots
Functioning warehousing and their geographical locations for contingency/pre-positioning of stocks are mapped (GIS) and deployment plan finalized and shared
Macro planning for OCV campaigns are developed and funding sources identified
National functioning cold chain equipment are mapped and quantified
At least 80% of Vaccinators listed out and received refresher training
At least 80% of latrines in hot spot areas have functioning hand hygiene stations
4 toilets/improved latrines available for OPD settings OR 1 toilet per 20 users for IPD in CTUs in hot spot areas
Community volunteers are trained in IEC messaging on Hygiene promotion and safe handling of food
WASH protocols and guidance documents are updated and available in at least 80% all health facilities
Safe and sufficient water is available at community level according to population in hotspots
Designated officer for food safety in hotspots areas
At least 80% of health facilities in hot spot areas have functional medical waste management system
The country has defined a package of essential health services (EHS) at the national and sub-national levels
The country has developed and operationalized plans/procedures/guidelines for the continuity of essential health services during a cholera outbreak
The country has established a functional mechanism for monitoring the continuity of essential health services
